knowledge_point.title: Evaluating Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}4xy\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
x=u,\,y=v,\,z=6-3u-2v
$$

for $0\le u\le \frac{5}{2}$ and $0\le v\le \frac{1}{2}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,6-3u-2v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(6-3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-3⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(6-3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}0 & -3 \\ 1 & -2\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}1 & -3 \\ 0 & -2\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,2,\,1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨3,\,2,\,1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9+4+1} \\  & =\sqrt{14}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =4xy\,{|}_{x=u\,y=v\,z=6-3u-2v} \\  & =4uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le \frac{5}{2},\,0\le v\le \frac{1}{2}\},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}4xy\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,4uv\sqrt{14}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{14}{∬}_{D}\,4uv\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{14}{\int }_{0}^{\frac{5}{2}}2u\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}}2v\,\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{14}\cdot [{u}^{2}]_{0}^{\frac{5}{2}}\cdot [{v}^{2}]_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{14}[\left(\frac{25}{4}\right)-(0)]\cdot [\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)-(0)] \\  & =\sqrt{14}\cdot \frac{25}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{25\sqrt{14}}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Evaluating Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}{x}^{2}-2yz\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
x=u+v,\,y=u,\,z=v
$$

for $-\frac{3}{2}\le u\le \frac{3}{2}$ and $-\frac{1}{2}\le v\le 0.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,u,\,v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,-1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨1,\,-1,\,-1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1+1} \\  & =\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & ={x}^{2}-2yz\,{|}_{x=u+v\,y=u\,z=v} \\  & =(u+v)^{2}-2uv \\  & ={u}^{2}+{v}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-\frac{3}{2}\le u\le \frac{3}{2\},\,-\frac{1}{2}\le v\le 0},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}{x}^{2}-2yz\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,({u}^{2}+{v}^{2})\sqrt{3}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{3}{∬}_{D}\,{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{3}{\int }_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{0}({\int }_{-\frac{3}{2}}^{\frac{3}{2}}{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}\,\text{d}u)\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{3}{\int }_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{0}{[\frac{{u}^{3}}{3}+u{v}^{2}]}_{u=-\frac{3}{2}}^{u=\frac{3}{2}}\,\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{3}{\int }_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{0}[(\frac{3v^{2}}{2}+\frac{9}{8})-(\left(-\frac{3v^{2}}{2}\right)+\left(-\frac{9}{8}\right))]\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{3}{\int }_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{0}\frac{9}{4}+3{v}^{2}\,\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{3}{[\frac{9}{4}v+{v}^{3}]}_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{0} \\  & =\sqrt{3}[(0+0)-(\left(-\frac{9}{8}\right)+\left(-\frac{1}{8}\right))] \\  & =\sqrt{3}(0+0)-\sqrt{3}(-\frac{9}{8}-\frac{1}{8}) \\  & =\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Evaluating Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}(xy+z)\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
x=u+v,\,y=u-v,\,z=0
$$

for $1\le u\le 2$ and $-\frac{1}{2}\le v\le 0.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,u-v,\,0⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,-2⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨0,\,0,\,-2⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+0+4} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =xy+z\,{|}_{x=u+v\,y=u-v\,z=0} \\  & =(u+v)(u-v) \\  & ={u}^{2}-{v}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,1\le u\le 2,\,-\frac{1}{2}\le v\le 0\},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}(xy+z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\cdot 2\,\text{d}A \\  & =2{∬}_{D}\,({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & =2{\int }_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{0}({\int }_{1}^{2}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\,\text{d}u)\text{d}v \\  & =2{\int }_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{0}{[\frac{{u}^{3}}{3}-{v}^{2}u]}_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}v \\  & =2{\int }_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{0}[((-2v^{2})+\frac{8}{3})-((-v^{2})+\frac{1}{3})]\text{d}v \\  & =2{\int }_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{0}(\frac{7}{3}-{v}^{2})\text{d}v \\  & =2{[\frac{7v}{3}-\frac{{v}^{3}}{3}]}_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{0} \\  & =2[(0+0)-(\left(-\frac{7}{6}\right)+\frac{1}{24})] \\  & =2[0+0-(-\frac{7}{6}+\frac{1}{24})] \\  & =\frac{9}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}2xz\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
x=u,\,y=u+v,\,z=2v
$$

for $0\le u\le \frac{5}{2}$ and $0\le v\le \frac{1}{2}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,u+v,\,2v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,-2,\,1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨2,\,-2,\,1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+4+1} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =2xz\,{|}_{x=u\,y=u+v\,z=2v} \\  & =2u(2v) \\  & =4uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le \frac{5}{2\},\,0\le v\le \frac{1}{2}},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}2xz\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,4uv\cdot 3\,\text{d}A \\  & =3{∬}_{D}\,4uv\,\text{d}A \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{\frac{5}{2}}2u\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}}2v\,\text{d}v \\  & =3\cdot [{u}^{2}]_{0}^{\frac{5}{2}}\cdot [{v}^{2}]_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \\  & =3[\left(\frac{25}{4}\right)-(0)]\cdot [\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)-(0)] \\  & =3\cdot \frac{25}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{75}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Evaluating Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}x(y+z)\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
x=2u,\,y=-3v,\,z=4v
$$

for $0\le u\le \frac{5}{2}$ and $0\le v\le \frac{1}{2}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2u,\,-3v,\,4v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-3v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-3v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-3,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}0 & 0 \\ -3 & 4\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -3\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-8,\,-6⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨0,\,-8,\,-6⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-8)^{2}+(-6)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+64+36} \\  & =\sqrt{100} \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =x(y+z)\,{|}_{x=2u\,y=-3v\,z=4v} \\  & =2u(-3v+4v) \\  & =2uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le \frac{5}{2\},\,0\le v\le \frac{1}{2}},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}x(y+z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2uv\cdot 10\,\text{d}A \\  & =5{∬}_{D}\,4uv\,\text{d}A \\  & =5{\int }_{0}^{\frac{5}{2}}2u\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}}2v\,\text{d}v \\  & =5\cdot [{u}^{2}]_{0}^{\frac{5}{2}}\cdot [{v}^{2}]_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \\  & =5[\left(\frac{25}{4}\right)-(0)]\cdot [\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)-(0)] \\  & =5\cdot \frac{25}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{125}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Evaluating Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}({x}^{2}-{z}^{2})\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
x=2u+v,\,y=2u-2v,\,z=u+2v
$$

for $-\frac{3}{2}\le u\le \frac{3}{2}$ and $-\frac{1}{2}\le v\le 0.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2u+v,\,2u-2v,\,u+2v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u-2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,2,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u-2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-2,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 2 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -2 & 2\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ -2 & 2\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,-3,\,-6⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨6,\,-3,\,-6⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{6}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+(-6)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36+9+36} \\  & =\sqrt{81} \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & ={x}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,{|}_{x=2u+v\,y=2u-2v\,z=u+2v} \\  & =(2u+v)^{2}-(u+2v)^{2} \\  & =3{u}^{2}-3{v}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-\frac{3}{2}\le u\le \frac{3}{2\},\,-\frac{1}{2}\le v\le 0},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}{x}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,(3{u}^{2}-3{v}^{2})\cdot 9\,\text{d}A \\  & =9{∬}_{D}\,(3{u}^{2}-3{v}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & =9{\int }_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{0}({\int }_{-\frac{3}{2}}^{\frac{3}{2}}(3{u}^{2}-3{v}^{2})\,\text{d}u)\text{d}v \\  & =9{\int }_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{0}{[{u}^{3}-3{v}^{2}u]}_{-\frac{3}{2}}^{\frac{3}{2}}\,\text{d}v \\  & =9{\int }_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{0}[(\left(-\frac{9v^{2}}{2}\right)+\frac{27}{8})-(\frac{9v^{2}}{2}+\left(-\frac{27}{8}\right))]\text{d}v \\  & =9{\int }_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{0}(\frac{27}{4}-9{v}^{2})\text{d}v \\  & =9\cdot [\frac{27v}{4}-3{v}^{3}]_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{0} \\  & =9[(0+0)-(\left(-\frac{27}{8}\right)+\frac{3}{8})] \\  & =9\cdot (3) \\  & =27.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}(2x+y+z)\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2u-v,\,3u+2,\,u+2v⟩
$$

 
over the domain $D=\{(u,v)\,:\,1\le u\le 2,\,-\frac{1}{2}\le v\le 0\}.$

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{70}.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$

$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(2x+y+z)\,{|}_{x=2u-v\,y=3u+2\,z=u+2v} \\  & =2(2u-v)+(3u+2)+(u+2v) \\  & =8u+2\end{aligned}

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =6xyz\,{|}_{x=u\,y=u+v\,z=v} \\  & =6(u)(u+v)(v) \\  & =6({u}^{2}v+u{v}^{2})\end{aligned}

$$

$$

 
over the domain $D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le \frac{5}{2},\,0\le v\le \frac{1}{2}\}.$

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=2\sqrt{10}.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=2\sqrt{10}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(xy+xz)\,{|}_{x=u\,y=2v\,z=6v} \\  & =(u)(2v)+(u)(6v) \\  & =8uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,8uv\cdot 2\sqrt{10}\,\text{d}A \\  & =16\sqrt{10}{∬}_{D}\,uv\,\text{d}A \\  & =16\sqrt{10}{\int }_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\frac{5}{2}}uv\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & =16\sqrt{10}({\int }_{0}^{\frac{5}{2}}u\,\text{d}u)({\int }_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}}v\,\text{d}v) \\  & =16\sqrt{10}\cdot {[\frac{{u}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{\frac{5}{2}}\cdot {[\frac{{v}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \\  & =16\sqrt{10}[\left(\frac{25}{8}\right)-(0)]\cdot [\left(\frac{1}{8}\right)-(0)] \\  & =16\sqrt{10}\cdot \frac{25}{8}\cdot \frac{1}{8} \\  & =\frac{25\sqrt{10}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
